checks.detail: The unit-normal finite coordinate derivative follows actual Gaussian normal disintegration and endpoint-local FTC, retaining every other inequality.
Nonunit normalization rescales the selected threshold by sigma and retains exactly the Gaussian PDF/sigma Jacobian.
A retained zero normal at nonzero threshold is locally always satisfied or locally makes the event empty; its actual first derivative is zero and continuous nearby.
The local geometric regularity condition is open; differentiability and derivative continuity are genuine and feed the checked local partials theorem.
No full normal-family linear independence, invertible covariance, or upper bound on the number of faces is required.
The radial trace identity uses actual log-scaling of a bounded hard indicator and the actual CDF Frechet derivative, with the negative sign and all retained finite terms correct.
The first-moment boundary law uses actual Cameron-Martin/MGF translation; dot(nonunit-normal,v) multiplies a derivative already carrying inverse-sigma normalization.

scope_qualification: These are local calculus/support results. The finite regularity premise is ordinary affine noncoincidence and is independently discharged volume-almost-everywhere for the actual residual family by ae_residualThresholdRegularity; no full H1 quantitative estimate is claimed.
